title: Clamp Retry-After Window and formalize tool-call idempotency contract for OpenAI shim
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Motivation: Clients of the OpenAI compatibility shim and our native API have been handling rate-limit responses inconsistently due to differing header shapes and an unbounded Retry-After policy coming from the gateway. This causes two classes of customer-facing issues: (1) clients requeue aggressively on short windows and get immediate subsequent 429s, or conversely back off for excessively long windows; (2) tool/function call semantics that trigger side effects have no well-defined client-facing idempotency guidance, which makes it hard for callers to safely retry streaming or tool-invocation failures.

This PR does three things in a single change set to improve API robustness and cross-compatibility: 1) Clamp and canonize Retry-After semantics across the gateway and OpenAI shim, 2) Standardize response header names and structured error codes for rate/limit conflicts, and 3) Add a documented idempotency contract for tool/function calls exposed via function-calling tooling to make retries safe and observable.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a configurable Retry-After clamping policy in gateway/rate_limiter.go. By default Retry-After values returned to clients are clamped to [1s, 120s] unless tenant overrides are configured. The gateway still observes internal longer windows for internal routing, but the outward-facing header is normalized to prevent pathological client backoffs.
- Canonicalized rate headers in adapter/openai_headers.go: we now set both X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After, plus an optional X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch seconds) for callers that prefer deterministic resets. Header names are intentionally additive to preserve OpenAI-compat where present.
- Introduced structured error codes (api_error.code) on HTTP JSON error responses and an OpenAI-mapping table so that clients get consistent strings like "rate_limit.exceeded", "rate_limit.in_flight", "tool.execution_conflict", and "request.timeout". The response shape maintains the OpenAI-compatible fields but adds a top-level "code" key for programmatic checks.
- Tool/function calling: added an explicit idempotency contract for tool invocations (api/tool_invoker.go). Callers may opt-in to a per-invocation Idempotency-Key header. When present, the invoker guarantees at-least-once semantics but deduplicates executions for the lifetime of the stored key (default 5 minutes). If the tool is side-effectful and cannot be deduplicated, the invoker returns 409 with code "tool.execution_conflict" and details explaining the partial state and a suggested retry window.
- Streaming stability: improved backpressure handling in the OpenAI shim streaming adapter (adapter/streaming_backpressure.go) so that Retry-After is not emitted mid-stream; instead we surface well-formed terminal error events with structured codes. This reduces ambiguous client behaviour on half-closed streams.
- Tests and docs: added e2e tests for corner cases and updated docs in docs/openai_compat.md and docs/tool_idempotency.md.

Checklist (approx):
- [x] Gateway clamping implementation and feature flag
- [x] OpenAI header canonicalization and compatibility layer
- [x] Structured error codes + mapping table
- [x] Tool invoker idempotency flow + 409 semantics
- [x] Streaming adapter adjustments to avoid mid-stream Retry-After emissions
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs (OpenAI shim + tooling idempotency)

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing clients will continue to receive OpenAI-compatible fields. We avoid removing headers; instead we add canonical ones. The only visible change is the clamped Retry-After maximum and the presence of a programmatic "code" field in error responses. To minimize surprise we gate the clamping behind a runtime toggle that is enabled for new tenants and rolled out to existing tenants over 2 weeks.

Operational notes:
- Default clamping upper bound is configurable via env REDWOOD_RATE_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS (default 120). Tenants with strict regulatory requirements can opt out via tenant config.
- Tool idempotency store uses our existing short-lived cache (KV store) with a 5 minute TTL default; this is tunable per-tenant for high-volume tool callers.

Why this approach?
- Clamping aligns client semantics and avoids extreme backoffs.
- Structured codes give deterministic programmatic behaviour for SDKs and customers migrating from other APIs.
- Explicit idempotency contract makes tool retries safe without forcing consumers to build custom locking.

Related work: Linear ENG-5123 (rate semantics audit), PM-241 (compatibility migration), prior PRs that touched Retry-After and idempotency surfaced behaviour.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit and integration tests added under tests/ (simulate short/long Retry-After, tool retry races, streaming mid-error).
- Feature-flagged rollout to a small subset of tenants, followed by metrics observation (rate.limit.adjustment, tool.idempotency.hits, streaming.errors).

If anything needs to be split out before merge (size concerns), I can extract the header canonicalization into a follow-up, but reviewers requested keeping the end-to-end semantics visible in this single PR for quicker verification in the staging environment.

b2c7c8a feat(adapter): add X-RateLimit-Reset and canonical error code mapping for OpenAI shim
c3d2e1f feat(tool): implement idempotency-key handling and dedupe store for tool invocations
d4e5f6a fix(stream): avoid emitting Retry-After mid-stream and surface terminal structured errors
e5f6a7b test(docs): add e2e cases and docs updates
review_comments: Miguel Torres (2025-07-21): Strongly 👍 on clamping. One operational question: can we emit both Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Reset? Author: yes, both are emitted; Retry-After is clamped and Reset is authoritative epoch time.

Laura Chen (2025-07-22): Tool idempotency looks good, but we need an explicit note in docs that 409 semantics may include partial execution metadata. Author: added docs/tool_idempotency.md with suggested client behavior and example responses.

Samir Bhandari (2025-07-24): CI flake on e2e intermittent; re-ran and green. Also requested a small change to log metric when dedupe hits occur. Author: added metric tool.idempotency.hits in pkg/metrics.
Miguel Torres (2025-07-28): Approved after minor nits addressed.
merge_commit_message: Clamp Retry-After + canonical headers + tool idempotency: establish cross-shim retry semantics and structured error codes
release_notes:
- Normalize rate-limit headers and clamp Retry-After to an adjustable default max (120s).
- Add X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch) and stable error code field for programmatic checks.
- Define idempotency-key semantics for tool/function calls; returns 409 with code 'tool.execution_conflict' for non-dedupable conflicts.
- Streaming adapter no longer emits Retry-After mid-stream; terminal structured errors are emitted instead.
notes_for_ops: Rollout is feature-flagged. Watch metrics: rate.limit.adjustment, tool.idempotency.hits, streaming.errors. Default Retry-After max is 120s; change via REDWOOD_RATE_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS env or tenant opt-out.
post_merge_followups: Consider extracting header canonicalization into a tiny follow-up for faster landing if needed
Add longer TTL option for tenants that need extended idempotency windows
ci_log_summary: All CI checks passed after second run: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), e2e (pass)
notes_for_SDKs: SDKs should prefer checking top-level 'code' on errors for programmatic handling; SDKs may map 'rate_limit.exceeded' to backoff strategies and treat 'tool.execution_conflict' as non-idempotent conflict with suggested retry delay extracted from error details.
